messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2422501234 — serving-runtime alert: elevated OOMs + container crashloops in eu-west-prod cluster. Observed spike in pod restarts across the inference pool, autoscaler activity high (rapid scale up/down). Impact: latency +2.1s p95 for some routes, ~5% 5xx rate. Pager routed to @oncall_elise.

oncall_elise: taking pager — joining Zoom in 2.

raj: saw kube events showing NodeNotReady flapping and kubelet restarts on gputype-rtx nodes. Crashloop backoff logs attached to a few pods: 
```
E tensorflow	something: CUDA out of memory: trying to allocate 2.1G
containerd: process exited with status 137
```
Looks like memory pressure during rapid attach of many pods.

diego: customer impact: I've already flagged 3 customers with production traffic seeing 502/503s on model endpoints; one is a high-volume realtime customer. Notified account team.

oncall_elise: quick triage notes: autoscaler has been flapping from 20 -> 60 -> 22 nodes over last 10m. Scaling cooldown may be too short and the runtime pods can't warm the KV cache quickly, so subsequent instances get heavy memory usage and OOM. Initial mitigation plan: pause autoscaler, scale manually to a safe count, and drain obviously bad nodes.

katie: agree. On eu-west cluster I recommend scaling to 48 nodes (observed stable at ~45 last week) and set autoscaler min/max to 44/60 after stable. Also increase node stabilization window to 10m.

eng-runtime: adding: runtime teams saw memory spikes at model load due to repeated cold starts. We can temporarily enable prefix-KV reuse across warmers to cut memory usage per-attach, but that's a 2-step change. Immediate: stop churn.

oncall_elise: executing mitigation now: 
- disabling cluster-autoscaler (kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}')
- manual scale node pool to 48 via cloudops console and wait for nodeready
- cordon/evict crashlooping pods on nodes with repeated OOM (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data)
- put runtime route fallback policy into conservative mode (route smaller model variant) for impacted customer lanes

sre-shift: heads up: after we disable autoscaler some tenants may see slower burst capacity but fewer OOMs. I'm good to help with node drains.

raj: I'm tailing logs: there's a repeating pattern: autoscaler spins up many pods, those attempt model load simultaneously, GPU memory allocation fails and container exits with 137. Then autoscaler interprets high pending demand and spins up again -> feedback loop.

oncall_elise: applied node-scale to 48; nodes are joining. Evicting 6 nodes with repeated OOMs; new pods are being scheduled. Monitoring.

diego: customer update: sent temporary advisory to affected customers — routing them to degraded mode and explaining we're mitigating; major SRE oncall is in the loop.

eng-runtime: small tweak applied to podSpec: set GOMAXPROCS-style env and reduce prefetch workers for model load in the interim (will revert after stability). Redeploying 6 pods now.

sre-shift: observed p95 tail latency coming down from +2.1s to +600ms on monitored routes. Error rate dropping to ~1.2%. Good signal.

oncall_elise: reenable autoscaler only after stabilization window of 20m and after bumping scale stabilization config. For now we'll keep it off.

katie: can we add a short-term op to change cluster-autoscaler config: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --scale-up-delay=45s? That should slow feedback.

eng-runtime: noted. Also we need to add a warmup job that streams KV cache entries during scale events. Filed task INF-8812.

raj: postmortem seeds: immediate cause = rapid autoscaler churn causing many cold model loads -> GPU OOM -> container restarts -> autoscaler interprets sustained demand -> repeat. Contributing: aggressive autoscale cooldown/stabilization settings, and lack of warmup for KV cache/model weights.

oncall_elise: handing back pager to @sre-shift — cluster stable for now, autoscaler off, manual scale in place. Will follow up in incident doc and link to INF-8812.

sre-shift: taking handoff. tagging owners for follow-ups: @eng-runtime on warmup design, @platform for autoscaler config audit, @support for customer comms follow-up.

eng-runtime: we'll schedule a canary test for the warmup flow and a load test that simulates rapid scale events.

katie: thanks all. next steps: 1) draft incident timeline + impact numbers, 2) change autoscaler flags and stabilization window, 3) implement KV warmup + reduced model cold-start memory profile, 4) post-incident review + SLA outreach. I'll create the ticket and assign.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2422501234 status -> mitigated (72 minutes). Follow-up: create postmortem and link to internal doc.

sre-shift: closing thread update: monitoring will stay at elevated for 2h. If no regressions, we'll re-enable controlled autoscaling tomorrow with updated flags.
